name: THREAT Matrix
full_name: Tactical Human Risk Enumeration and Adversary Taxonomy Matrix

matrices.boundary_rule: Each tactic in this catalog is placed in exactly one matrix at authoring time, determined by the adversary's primary objective. The WHAT/WHY/WHERE separation is the disambiguation tool for the People matrix specifically; for Facility, Organization, and Infrastructure, WHERE collapses into WHAT and the boundary is set by what the adversary's primary objective targets. Motivation lives in actor profiles, not in matrix placement. Real-world incidents may legitimately invoke tactics from multiple matrices simultaneously; cross-matrix coverage is expressed through the Detection Mesh via indicator correlates_with references. When a downstream consumer requires a single primary-matrix call per incident, default to the matrix containing the tactic that achieved the adversary's terminal objective; ties broken by precedence People > Facilities > Organizations > Infrastructure. Where the adversary's primary objective is uncertain or unknown, primary-matrix placement defaults to the matrix containing the tactic that produced the most observable consequence; the incident-level confidence of this inference is annotated separately via primary_objective_evidence_tier. Consumers may override.

tactics.name: Target Selection
tactics.notes: Who, what, and why this target. Precedes all reconnaissance. Actor evaluates candidate targets against attack objectives — relationship to grievance, symbolic value, access feasibility, and vulnerability. The decision to focus on a specific target — whether a named individual, a role or identity category, an affinity group, or an indiscriminate set — marks the transition from general grievance to targeted threat.
tactics.cpn_notes: Social media, LinkedIn, data brokers, and OSINT tools are primary sources for modern target selection. Digital footprint analysis can produce a detailed vulnerability assessment before any physical reconnaissance occurs.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor articulates specific grievance tied to a named individual, attributing personal harm or injustice to that person's actions or role
Threat actor conducts sustained online research into a specific individual's personal details, schedule, residence, workplace, family members, or daily routines
Threat actor repeatedly returns to grievance-related topics about a specific individual in conversations, writings, or social media posts, with increasing frequency or intensity over time
Threat actor communicates intent regarding a specific individual to a third party, including statements about wanting to harm, confront, or 'make them pay'
Threat actor researches prior attacks against similar targets, studying methodology, outcomes, and media coverage of previous incidents
Insider threat actor accesses personnel records, organizational charts, or executive travel schedules outside the scope of their job function

countermeasures.measure: Implement digital footprint reduction program for protected individuals including social media privacy hardening, data broker opt-out services, and personal information removal from public databases
countermeasures.limitations: Cannot eliminate all public records. Determined adversary can still aggregate partial information from multiple sources.

countermeasures.measure: Deploy social media monitoring for mentions of protected individuals, organizational leaders, and key personnel across public platforms
countermeasures.limitations: Only captures public posts. Encrypted messaging and private communications are not visible. False positive rate is high without human analyst review.

countermeasures.measure: Establish anonymous reporting channel for employees and associates to report concerning statements, fixation behaviors, or grievance escalation without fear of retaliation
countermeasures.limitations: Effectiveness depends on organizational trust and reporting culture. Anonymous tips require corroboration before action.

countermeasures.measure: Conduct proactive threat assessment briefings for individuals in high-visibility or high-risk roles, covering personal security awareness, digital hygiene, and when to report concerning contacts
countermeasures.limitations: Briefings raise awareness but do not prevent a determined actor from conducting research. Must be refreshed periodically to maintain vigilance.

countermeasures.measure: Implement access controls on personnel databases, executive calendars, and organizational directories with logging and anomaly alerting for access outside job scope
countermeasures.limitations: Insiders with legitimate access may not trigger alerts. Requires baseline behavior modeling to detect anomalies effectively.

response_protocols.trigger: Single indicator of target-specific grievance or fixation detected through peer report, social media monitoring, or behavioral observation
response_protocols.action: Document the indicator in the threat management case tracking system. Assign a threat management team analyst for preliminary review. Gather context from available data sources within 5 business days. Determine if additional monitoring or assessment is warranted.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Second indicator from a different category (e.g., communication + digital research) detected for the same threat actor / targeted subject pair, or the threat actor's behavior escalates in intensity or specificity
response_protocols.legal_notes: Document observations factually. Do not characterize mental health status. Ensure reporting channel complies with organizational anti-retaliation policy. If the threat actor is an employee, consult HR before any direct engagement. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

response_protocols.trigger: Multiple correlated indicators across different categories detected for the same threat actor / targeted subject pair, or a single high-severity indicator (direct communication of intent to harm a specific individual)
response_protocols.action: Convene threat management team within 24 hours. Conduct formal threat assessment using structured professional judgment. Implement protective measures for the identified targeted subject (awareness briefing, security posture increase, route variation guidance). Initiate enhanced monitoring of the threat actor across available data sources. Notify law enforcement if the threat is credible and specific.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Threat actor acquires means (weapon, access credential, vehicle) or demonstrates capability and proximity to the targeted subject. Threat actor's behavior meets the threshold for imminent risk.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Threat management team assessment is a protected security function. Coordinate with legal counsel before initiating any surveillance of the threat actor. If law enforcement is notified, document the basis for the notification. Ensure targeted-subject protective measures do not inadvertently disclose the investigation to the threat actor. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

response_protocols.trigger: Threat actor confirmed to have means, motive, and proximity to the targeted subject, with behavioral indicators suggesting imminent action (energy burst, last resort framing, final act behaviors)
response_protocols.action: Activate protective detail for the targeted subject immediately. Coordinate with law enforcement for threat actor interdiction or interview. Brief executive leadership. Implement emergency security measures at the targeted subject's residence and workplace. If the threat actor is an insider, execute immediate access revocation across all physical and digital systems.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Threat actor initiates approach to the targeted subject or breaches security perimeter. Transition to active threat response protocols.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Coordinate all interdiction actions through law enforcement. Ensure any access revocation follows established procedures to preserve evidence and protect against wrongful termination claims. Document the imminent threat assessment that triggered emergency measures. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

tactics.field_notes: Target Selection is the point where a vague or specific grievance lands on a named person. The threat actor's attention then reshapes around that individual — their schedule, where they live, their family, their daily routine. Inside an organization, the parallel signal is a threat actor pulling records that have little to nothing to do with their job: the personnel file, the target's calendar, and project information. The behavioral tell is simple — the grievance locks onto one person and stays there.
observed_contexts: former employee whose written grievance shifts from policy complaints to a specific manager's name and continues escalating in social media posts
fixated threat actor conducting digital research on a specific executive's residence, family routine, and travel pattern over weeks
insider with legitimate role access pulling personnel records, calendars, and travel itineraries that fall outside their declared job function
domestic stalking case progressing from generalized harassment to targeted research on the targeted subject's daily movements
[literature: NTAC-MASS-2021 case pattern — pre-attack target grievance narrowed to a single named individual identified weeks or months before mobilization]

credibility.criteria: Credibility of a Target Selection finding rises with convergence — separate indicator types pointing at the same named individual within overlapping timeframes — with a trajectory observed over time rather than a single moment, and with recoverable evidence that does not depend on accurate witness recall. It falls with single uncorroborated reports, targeting that stays diffuse, an unaddressed ordinary explanation, and reporters whose stake in the matter could distort what they pass on.
high_signal_anchors: Convergence across indicator types onto one named subject — grievance expression, target research, and intent disclosure independently pointing at the same individual; no single indicator carries this and it is the strongest credibility pattern in the tactic.
An observed trajectory rather than a snapshot — the concern is documented as a pattern across weeks or months, so the assessor is weighing a trend, not a remark.

Recoverable corroborating evidence — retained search activity, written or posted content, or access records that physically tie the actor to the subject and survive independent of how well a witness remembers.
First-hand disclosure fidelity — a named person who directly received an account of the actor's interest and can relay its content, context, and the individual named, rather than second-hand summary.
Operational specificity in what is reported — the actor's attention is described as fixed on a specific named individual and concrete personal detail, not a generalized complaint.
Reporter standing aligned with accuracy — the account reaches the assessor through a person or channel with no structural stake in the outcome and no incentive to amplify.
low_signal_anchors: A lone uncorroborated report — one tip, no second indicator, and a source who cannot be re-contacted to test it.
Targeting that stays diffuse — hostility expressed toward a role, an institution, or a category, with no specific individual resolved.
An ordinary explanation left standing — the behavior fits a mundane account (a genuine workplace dispute, ordinary curiosity) that the assessment never actually ruled out.
Reporter stake that could distort — the person raising the concern is inside an active dispute, rivalry, or proceeding with the subject, so the account may be inflated.
Reconstructive recall — a long gap between observation and report, where detail may have been retrofitted to a threatening narrative after the fact.
A static, isolated mention — a one-time expression with no recurrence, no intensification, and no second behavior to corroborate it.

capability.criteria: Capability is generally a low-signal dimension for Target Selection — most of the tactic is grievance expression, disclosure, and research, none of which demonstrate tradecraft, and open disclosure of intent is closer to an operational-security failure than a competence. Capability registers only where the actor draws on a position of legitimate access used beyond its scope, conducts research that exceeds casual lookups, or shows discipline in compartmentalizing what they gather. It stays low wherever behavior is conspicuous, undisciplined, and trivially attributable.
high_signal_anchors: A position of access exploited for target intelligence — the actor reaches information about the subject through legitimate standing used outside its proper scope, a capability ordinary actors do not have.
Research that exceeds casual lookup — structured compilation of a subject's pattern of life, or methodical study of how earlier attacks were conducted, rather than surface searches anyone could run.
Operational-security discipline — the actor gathers intelligence while withholding intent, works through intermediaries, or avoids channels that would attribute the activity.
Synthesis rather than collection — the actor is organizing what they gather into an actionable picture of the subject, not merely accumulating fragments.
Sustained, methodical effort — target development carried out deliberately and in an organized way over time, rather than impulsively.
low_signal_anchors: Open disclosure of intent or grievance — the actor broadcasts hostility where it is readily heard, demonstrating no concern for concealment.
Casual public lookups only — all research is surface-level and requires no skill or non-obvious sourcing.
Trivially attributable activity — research and expression conducted under the actor's own identity, on channels that tie straight back to them.
Impulsive, disorganized expression — grievance vented without structure, method, or any sign of sustained development.
No sign of synthesis — fragments of information about the subject accumulate with no indication they are being organized toward action.

intent.criteria: Intent is the primary dimension of Target Selection — this is the tactic in which intent forms and first becomes observable. Intent rises as a grievance narrows from a diffuse sense of injustice onto a specific named individual, as fixation recurs with increasing frequency or intensity, as the actor articulates a desire to harm, and as grievance is paired with research into the subject's life. It falls with a static non-escalating complaint, targeting that never resolves to an individual, a verifiable benign purpose, and grievance that is unaccompanied by any target-development behavior.
high_signal_anchors: A grievance that has narrowed onto a person — a sense of injustice that has resolved from a diffuse complaint to a specific named individual held singularly responsible.
An escalation trajectory — fixation on the subject recurring with rising frequency or intensity over time; the trend itself, not any single expression, is the signal.

Intent voiced as a concrete act rather than a feeling — the assessor weighs a stated wish to harm, confront, or punish the subject differently from generalized anger, and weights it further when it was disclosed to someone with no reason to invent it.
Grievance paired with target development — hostility toward the subject and information-gathering about the subject co-occurring; the pairing is intent-diagnostic in a way neither behavior is alone.

Movement from grievance toward method — the actor's attention shifting from why the subject deserves harm toward how harm would be carried out, whether through study of comparable cases, interest in weapons, or attention to the subject's vulnerabilities.
Attribution of singular blame — the actor frames one named individual as the unique cause of their grievance, the framing that precedes target fixation.
low_signal_anchors: A static grievance — a complaint expressed once, with no recurrence, escalation, or intensification.
Diffuse targeting — hostility toward a role, an institution, or a category, with no named individual.
A verifiable benign purpose — the contact or research has a checkable legitimate basis (professional duty, genuine dispute resolution, ordinary interest).
Grievance without target development — a complaint voiced but unaccompanied by any research, observation, or intel-gathering directed at the subject.
Expression treated as catharsis — venting that the actor and those around them experience as letting off steam, with no directed follow-through.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity is generally a low-signal dimension for Target Selection — grievance and intent expression resolve nothing about whether the actor can actually reach the subject. Opportunity registers where the actor has acquired pattern-of-life intelligence (the subject's routine, schedule, residence, or regular venues) or is drawing on a position of access that places them in or near the subject's environment. It stays low where the actor holds only a grievance, where targeting is diffuse, or where what the actor knows is generic and public rather than the operational picture that resolves a reachable window.
high_signal_anchors: Pattern-of-life intelligence acquired — the actor has compiled the subject's routine, schedule, residence, or regular venues, the informational form of opportunity.
A position of access being drawn on — the actor occupies legitimate standing that reaches into the subject's environment and is using it beyond its scope.
Timing intelligence resolved — the actor has obtained the subject's schedule or travel pattern, narrowing toward when the subject is predictably reachable.
Demonstrated environmental reach — research or access that shows working knowledge of the subject's physical or organizational surroundings, not just biographical facts.
Proximity through role or relationship — the actor's standing as a colleague, neighbour, or associate already places them in or adjacent to the subject's environment.
Intelligence converging toward a reachable window — separate research threads narrowing together onto a specific time or place the subject is accessible.
low_signal_anchors: Grievance without environmental knowledge — hostility expressed with no sign the actor knows anything about the subject's life or surroundings.
Diffuse targeting — no specific subject, so no opportunity to resolve.
Generic study with no subject-specific reach — research into prior cases or general method, carrying no operational picture of this subject.
No indication of reach — nothing suggests the actor can get into or near the subject's environment.
A public-information picture only — what the actor knows is all generic and openly available, not the operational pattern of life that resolves a window.
Intent unaccompanied by access — an explicit desire to harm with no indication of how the actor would reach the subject at all.

false_positive_context.criteria: Several ordinary activities resemble Target Selection indicators on the surface — workplace conflict produces grievance language, ordinary curiosity produces lookups of an individual, and genuine disputes produce intense and recurring complaint. What separates a false positive from a concern is whether the grievance has a verifiable ordinary basis, whether targeting stays diffuse rather than resolving onto a named individual marked for harm, whether research has a checkable legitimate purpose, and whether the pattern lacks the escalation and operational specificity that distinguish target development from ordinary grievance.
contexts: Ordinary workplace or interpersonal conflict — grievance language arising from a real, documented dispute, where the complaint is about a situation or a decision and shows no narrowing toward a person marked for harm.
Legitimate research and professional duty — journalists, investigators, HR or legal staff, recruiters, and background-check professionals whose lookups of an individual have a checkable mandate.
Ordinary social curiosity — looking up a public figure, a former partner, a new colleague, or a neighbour out of non-threatening interest.
Protected grievance expression — people airing genuine complaints about an institution or a public figure as ordinary expression, with no specific individual singled out for harm.
Hobby and current-events interest — studying past attacks or incidents as a student, researcher, or media consumer, with no connection to a specific subject.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Target Selection findings sit at the foundation of the threat pathway: they establish whether a specific person is being selected as a target and whether intent is forming around them. Because this is the earliest tactic, the most important reading is trajectory — a static finding and the same finding recurring with rising intensity warrant very different responses. Tier determination rests on three factors: credibility per the credibility criteria, convergence across indicator types, and escalation over time. A single low-credibility finding with an available ordinary explanation sits at a monitoring tier. A single high-credibility finding — a specific named grievance, an explicit disclosure of intent to harm, or target intelligence drawn from exploited access — sits at an investigation tier. Convergence — grievance, research, and disclosure pointing together at the same named subject — sits at an elevation tier and should be treated as coordinated target development. Escalation — fixation intensifying despite intervening time or de-escalation effort — sits at a committed-actor tier and suggests movement toward mobilization. Findings that correlate with later-phase behavior elsewhere — surveillance, capability acquisition, rehearsal — warrant immediate response-protocol activation regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Multiple lower-tier findings correlating in time or against the same subject compose to a higher aggregate tier than any one warrants alone; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: the monitoring tier triggers logging and pattern-detection; the investigation tier triggers actor identification and an assessment of whether the subject should be notified; the elevation tier triggers a structured threat assessment and consideration of subject-protective measures; the committed-actor tier triggers defensive-posture coordination and law-enforcement liaison.

tactics.name: Subject Profiling
tactics.notes: Sustained pattern-of-life intelligence collection on a specific named person. Actor builds a behavioral and spatial model of the subject: daily schedule, regular locations, social relationships, personal routines, and response patterns. This tactic is ongoing — it does not complete before Phase 2 begins.
tactics.cpn_notes: Digital profile — social media activity, location check-ins, fitness tracker data, public records aggregation — often precedes and supplements physical surveillance. Apps that publicly share routes or check-ins provide operationally precise location intelligence.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor compiles personal information about the targeted subject including home address, family member names, daily routine, and known associates
Threat actor monitors the targeted subject's social media activity over an extended period, archiving posts, photos, location check-ins, and life events

Threat actor obtains or attempts to obtain the targeted subject's personal documents — financial records, medical information, family details — through public records pulls, OSINT tools, or pretextual contact
Threat actor cultivates contact with the targeted subject's coworkers, neighbors, or family members under cover stories to elicit information about routine, schedule, or personal vulnerabilities
Threat actor builds a profile of the targeted subject's vehicles, including make, model, license plates, parking pattern, and typical departure and arrival times
Threat actor researches the targeted subject's recurring off-work venues — gym, restaurants, places of worship, hobbies — to identify predictable presence outside protected environments

countermeasures.measure: Conduct digital footprint reduction for the targeted subject — data broker opt-outs, address record removal where legally permitted, social media privacy hardening — to reduce the profileable surface available to a threat actor
countermeasures.limitations: Public records (court filings, property records, voter registration) cannot be fully removed; partial reduction raises adversary effort but does not eliminate the surface

countermeasures.measure: Brief the targeted subject and immediate household on common social engineering pretexts and cover stories used to extract personal information from family members and associates
countermeasures.limitations: Awareness fades over time without refresh; family members under personal stress may still respond to plausible-sounding pretexts

countermeasures.measure: Establish reporting channels for coworkers, neighbors, and household members to flag concerning inquiries from strangers, suspicious cover stories, or unexpected approaches
countermeasures.limitations: Reporting threshold varies by individual and culture; many concerning approaches are dismissed as harmless at the time

countermeasures.measure: Deploy social media monitoring for mentions of the targeted subject, immediate family members, and recurring locations across public platforms
countermeasures.limitations: Captures only public posts; encrypted or private monitoring is not visible. False positive rate is high without analyst review

response_protocols.trigger: One or more Subject Profiling indicators reported (suspicious inquiries about the targeted subject's routine, social media archival pattern, attempted records pull on the targeted subject or immediate family)
response_protocols.action: Open or update the case file. Conduct a 5-business-day preliminary assessment that includes (a) corroboration of the observation, (b) identification of any candidate threat actor, (c) baseline review of recent contact reports involving the targeted subject and immediate household. Document all sourcing.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Profiling activity extends to immediate family members OR co-occurs with indicators from another Phase 1 tactic for the same threat actor
response_protocols.legal_notes: Document factually. Concerning inquiries from a stranger are not by themselves unlawful; the security response is corroboration and pattern detection, not adverse action. If the threat actor is identifiable and an employee, consult HR before any direct engagement. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

response_protocols.trigger: Multiple Subject Profiling indicators co-observed for the same threat actor, OR profiling extends to family members, OR concurrent indicators surface from other Phase 1 tactics
response_protocols.action: Convene the threat management team. Conduct full risk assessment using structured professional judgment. Brief the targeted subject and immediate household on operational security and reporting expectations. Implement digital footprint reduction. Notify protective operations. Consider law-enforcement liaison consult depending on jurisdiction.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Threat actor identified with apparent means OR direct contact attempt with the targeted subject OR family member OR escalation to physical surveillance.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Brief the targeted subject and household on the specific indicators observed without disclosing investigative methodology. Privacy implications of monitoring third-party communications (coworkers, neighbors) must be reviewed before action. Document the indicator constellation that drove escalation. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

tactics.field_notes: Subject Profiling is the tactic that turns 'a name' into 'a target file'. The threat actor is no longer just looking up an address; they are building a detailed picture of who the targeted subject is — who they live with, where their kids go to school, what gym they belong to, what time they leave for work. Operationally, this can resolve into two collection streams — human-source (a known or unknown individual striking up a conversation with a coworker about the targeted subject's family, or a self-described 'researcher' calling neighbors with thin or implausible cover stories) and digital (a sustained pattern of social media monitoring — not casual interest, but methodical archival of posts, photos, and check-ins over weeks or months). Most of Subject Profiling sits in Target Development; what bleeds into mobilization is the threat actor confirming current status and validating earlier assumptions before action.
observed_contexts: domestic violence case where the threat actor cultivated friendships with the targeted subject's coworkers to extract daily schedule and family routine
executive protection case where social media archival revealed a multi-year pattern of the threat actor monitoring the targeted subject's posts, including children's events and travel photos
stalking case progressing from public-records research to in-person inquiries with neighbors under contractor cover stories
fixated insider compiling profile of an executive's family members, vehicles, and weekend routine outside any job function
[literature: MELOY-TRAP18-2016 — pathway warning sign of pre-attack research and 'studying' of the intended targeted subject]

credibility.criteria: Credibility of a Subject Profiling finding rises with convergence across collection modalities — digital, insider, and physical observation independently building one coherent operational picture — with a profile that is actively maintained and updated over time, and with recoverable evidence that does not depend on witness recall. It falls with isolated single-modality lookups, collection that fits an ordinary explanation, scattered detail that never assembles into a picture, and reporters whose stake could distort the account.
high_signal_anchors: Convergence across collection modalities — digital monitoring, insider inquiry, and physical observation independently assembling the same operational picture of one subject; no single indicator carries this.
An actively maintained profile — the intelligence is being updated and extended over time rather than gathered once, indicating ongoing operational use.
Recoverable collection evidence — archived material, records-request trails, or observation notes that physically tie the actor to the subject and survive independent of how well a witness remembers.
Operational coherence of the detail — the gathered facts fit together into an actionable picture rather than sitting as scattered, unrelated fragments.
First-hand reporting of an elicitation approach — a named person who was approached can relay the questions asked, the pretext used, and the specific detail sought.
Reporter standing aligned with accuracy — the account reaches the assessor through a person or channel with no structural stake in the outcome.
low_signal_anchors: An isolated single-modality lookup — one search or one record pull, with no second collection thread and no pattern.
Collection consistent with an ordinary explanation — the gathered information fits a mundane account the assessment never actually ruled out.
Reporter stake that could distort — the person raising the concern is inside an active dispute or proceeding with the actor or the subject.
Reconstructive recall — a long gap between an elicitation or observation and the report, where detail may be retrofitted to a threatening narrative.
Scattered, incoherent detail — the information does not assemble into an operational picture and may reflect unfocused curiosity.
Unverifiable second-hand summary — the concern is a summary of a summary, with no first-hand collection witness reachable.

capability.criteria: Capability is a moderate-signal dimension for Subject Profiling — most collection is open-source compilation that requires little skill, but the tactic does surface real tradecraft where the actor reaches beyond open sources, sustains a cover story under scrutiny, coordinates collection across modalities, or synthesizes fragments into an operational picture. It stays low where collection is casual, single-modality, and trivially attributable.
high_signal_anchors: Reach beyond open sources — collection has obtained records or detail that are not publicly available, through pretext, records-request expertise, or specialized tooling.
A cover story that held under scrutiny — a person approached for information did not recognize the approach as unusual, indicating a durable pretext.
Collection coordinated across modalities — digital, insider, and physical threads pursued together and deliberately, not as incidental overlap.
Synthesis into an operational picture — the actor is organizing gathered detail into an actionable profile of routine, venues, and reachability, not merely accumulating it.
Sustained, methodical collection — profiling carried out deliberately and maintained over time rather than impulsively.
low_signal_anchors: Casual public lookups only — all collection is surface-level open-source material requiring no skill.
A cover story that failed on contact — the person approached immediately recognized the questioning as unusual.
Single-modality collection — only digital, or only physical, with no coordination across collection types.
Trivially attributable activity — collection conducted under the actor's own identity on channels that tie straight back to them.
Accumulation without synthesis — fragments gathered with no sign they are being organized toward an operational picture.

intent.criteria: Intent is a high-signal dimension for Subject Profiling — sustained, organized collection of a specific person's pattern of life is rarely idle, and this is the tactic in which intent moves from grievance into operational target development. Intent rises with the breadth and operational focus of the profile, with collection that narrows toward how and where the subject is reachable, and with profiling maintained over time. It falls with a single incidental lookup, collection with a verifiable benign purpose, and interest that stays biographical rather than operational.
high_signal_anchors: Breadth of the operational picture — collection spanning routine, associates, venues, and movement, assembling the picture an actor would need to act rather than to satisfy curiosity.
Collection focused on reachability — profiling that narrows toward where and when the subject is accessible, especially outside protected settings.
A profile maintained over time — collection sustained and kept current, indicating the picture is being held for use rather than gathered once.
Escalation from grievance into target development — profiling that follows, and is directed at, a subject the actor has already expressed hostility toward.
Operational rather than biographical focus — the detail gathered is the kind that enables action, not the kind that satisfies general interest in who the subject is.
Concealed collection — information gathered through pretext or cover rather than openly, signalling the actor's own awareness that the collection would not be sanctioned.
low_signal_anchors: A single incidental lookup — one search or record pull with no breadth, sustainment, or operational focus.
A verifiable benign purpose — the collection has a checkable legitimate basis such as a background check, professional duty, or genuine reconnection.
Biographical rather than operational interest — the detail gathered concerns who the subject is, not how or where they could be reached.
Collection not resolved onto a named subject — profiling-type activity with no specific individual in view.
Open, un-pretexted inquiry — questions asked openly and honestly, consistent with ordinary interest rather than concealed collection.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity is a high-signal dimension for Subject Profiling — this is the tactic in which the actor acquires the pattern-of-life intelligence that constitutes opportunity. Opportunity rises as collection resolves the subject's routine, predictable presence, and reachability outside protected settings, and as the actor draws on insider access or proximity to gather what an outsider could not. It falls where collection stays biographical, where the picture is generic and public, and where nothing indicates the actor can convert knowledge into reach.
high_signal_anchors: Pattern of life resolved — the actor has assembled the subject's routine, schedule, and movement patterns, the informational substance of opportunity.
Reachability outside protective cover resolved — collection has established where and when the subject is predictably present without protection.
Insider access drawn on for collection — the actor occupies legitimate standing, or has cultivated insider contacts, and is using them to gather target intelligence an outsider could not.
Movement intelligence resolved — the actor has worked out how the subject travels and when, converting abstract knowledge into concrete reachable moments.
Multiple collection threads converging on a window — digital, physical, and insider intelligence narrowing together onto specific reachable times or places.
Proximity through role or relationship being exploited — the actor's standing as a colleague, neighbour, or associate used to gather what distance would deny.
low_signal_anchors: Biographical collection only — the actor has gathered who the subject is, with nothing about routine or reachability.
A generic, public picture — what the actor knows is all openly available and does not resolve the operational pattern of life.
No movement or venue intelligence — collection carries no routine, schedule, venue, or movement detail.
No indication of reach — nothing suggests the actor can convert collected knowledge into physical proximity.
Collection not resolved onto a subject — profiling-type activity with no specific individual, so no opportunity to resolve.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many ordinary activities resemble Subject Profiling indicators on the surface — background checks compile personal information, recruiters and journalists research individuals, and people ordinarily come to know the routines of colleagues and neighbours. What separates a false positive from a concern is whether the collection has a verifiable legitimate purpose, whether it stays biographical rather than resolving operational reachability, whether it is conducted openly rather than under a cover story, and whether it is a one-time inquiry rather than a sustained and maintained profile.
contexts: Authorized background and due-diligence checks — employers, landlords, lenders, and licensed screeners compiling personal information under a checkable mandate, typically with the subject's awareness or consent.
Professional research duty — journalists, biographers, recruiters, and licensed investigators researching an individual within a legitimate, checkable assignment.
Ordinary social knowledge — colleagues, neighbours, and acquaintances who know one another's routines, vehicles, and regular venues through ordinary proximity rather than deliberate collection.
Genuine reconnection or relationship interest — people locating an old friend, a relative, or a prospective partner out of non-threatening interest.
Open public-records and genealogy interest — hobbyists, family historians, and researchers using public records and OSINT openly, with no specific individual marked for harm.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Subject Profiling findings show whether an actor is assembling the operational picture needed to reach a specific person. The key reading is the coherence and operational focus of that picture: scattered biographical lookups and a maintained, multi-modal operational profile warrant very different responses. Tier determination rests on three factors: credibility per the credibility criteria, the breadth and operational focus of the collection, and whether collection is sustained and maintained over time. A single low-credibility biographical lookup with an available ordinary explanation sits at a monitoring tier. A single high-credibility finding of operational collection — pattern of life resolved, predictable presence outside protective cover identified, or insider access drawn on — sits at an investigation tier. Convergence — digital, insider, and physical collection assembling the same operational picture — sits at an elevation tier and should be treated as coordinated target development. Collection that has resolved the subject's reachability outside protected settings sits at a committed-actor tier and suggests readiness to move toward mobilization. Findings that correlate with later-phase behavior elsewhere — surveillance, capability acquisition, rehearsal — warrant immediate response-protocol activation regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Multiple lower-tier findings correlating in time or against the same subject compose to a higher aggregate tier than any one warrants alone; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: the monitoring tier triggers logging and pattern-detection; the investigation tier triggers actor identification and an assessment of the subject's exposure; the elevation tier triggers a structured threat assessment and subject-protective measures, focused on the venues and routines the collection has resolved; the committed-actor tier triggers defensive-posture coordination and law-enforcement liaison.

tactics.name: Environmental Survey
tactics.notes: Physical site assessment of locations associated with the subject — residence, workplace, vehicle routes, regular venues. Actor builds a spatial model of environments where the subject is present and vulnerable. Distinct from Subject Profiling (which focuses on the person); this tactic focuses on the locations.
tactics.cpn_notes: Satellite imagery, Google Maps Street View, live webcams, and publicly posted photos and videos of locations augment or replace physical walkthroughs. High-resolution imagery can provide actionable access and egress analysis before the actor visits a location in person.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities, persistence over time, and recoverable evidence backing first-hand witness reports. Credibility falls when the source, the content, or the temporal pattern is thin, and when plausible benign explanations were never ruled out.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — multiple indicators across different observation modes against the same subject within overlapping timeframes.
Temporal persistence — observed pattern across weeks-to-months within any modality, not single-event.
Material evidence — documents, recovered imagery, browser history, public-records request logs that physically link the actor to the subject; does not require accurate witness recall.

First-hand witness fidelity — named witness directly interacted with the actor; high-resolution reporting payload covering question content, pretext used, actor description, contact mechanism, and timing.
Behavioral specificity — actor named the specific subject, specific addresses, or specific operational details.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — trained professional reporting through formal channel, not informal tip with potential agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single anonymous tip without corroboration; reporter cannot be re-contacted.
Content-specificity weakness — vague description without operational detail that could fit dozens of mundane explanations.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one-time observation with no follow-through or escalation.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has structural motivation to embellish (active custody dispute, professional rivalry, ongoing litigation).
Unrebutted mundane explanation — indicator pattern admits a plausible benign interpretation that investigation did not rule out.
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay so long that details may be retrofitted to the threat narrative rather than observed.

capability.criteria: Capability rises with operational discipline that produces observable tradecraft — concealment, coordination across modes, acquisition of materials beyond casual OSINT reach, and pretexts that hold up under scrutiny. Capability falls with conspicuous behavior, weak pretexts, single-modality reach, and discipline failures that breach the actor's operational cover.
high_signal_anchors: Covert imaging tradecraft — telephoto from concealment, drone usage, brief-duration captures, no observable return-pattern.
Multi-modal operational coordination — physical, digital, and insider efforts coordinated across overlapping timeframes; not incidental coincidence.

Restricted-material acquisition — documents obtained include non-public materials such as security camera diagrams or internal floor plans, requiring social engineering, insider exploitation, or specialized records-request capability.
Pretext durability — pretexts and cutouts hold up under witness scrutiny; witness initially did not recognize they were being elicited.
Counter-surveillance behaviors — actor varies routes, scans for defender patrols, identifies camera coverage.
Demonstrated technical capability — actor reads or analyzes acquired materials productively, such as engineering analysis of blueprints or operational sequencing from acquired schedules.
low_signal_anchors: Conspicuous posture — loitering at sightlines, obvious recording, lingering past observation needs.
No-concealment repetition — multiple visits with no observable pretext or concealment.
Pretext failure on initial contact — witness immediately recognized the questioning as unusual.
OSINT-only reach — all acquired materials are from publicly available sources; no operational reach beyond browser-and-public-records.
Single-modality recon — only digital or only physical; no coordination across modes.
Direct target-contact attempts — actor sought direct contact with target or immediate orbit, breaching operational discipline about exposure.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when behavior progresses from broad exploration toward operationally specific detail against a named target, and especially when the actor demonstrates retention of acquired material or pairs reconnaissance with stated grievance toward the subject. Intent falls with generic interest, encounters that don't escalate, and behavior that has a verifiable benign explanation.
high_signal_anchors: Behavioral progression broad-to-narrow — observable funnel from initial OSINT through narrowing focus to operational-detail acquisition.
Target-specific behavior — behavior concentrates on the named subject and specific subject-associated addresses.

Operational specificity in inquiry or document selection — asking about emergency exit routes, camera coverage gaps, shift-change windows; selecting blueprints, security diagrams, or schedule documents specifically.
Sustained attention to defender posture — actor tracks countermeasures over time and adapts; not a one-and-done observation.
Retention of acquired materials — photos archived, plans saved, notes maintained; suggests later operational use rather than passing curiosity.

Hostile attribution paired with recon — actor has expressed grievance, blame, or hostile attribution toward the subject AND is observed conducting reconnaissance against subject-associated locations. The combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Generic-interest behavior — broad neighborhood photography, ambient OSINT not pinned to specific subjects.
One-time encounter without escalation — observation occurred but no follow-through or pattern emerged.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — journalist credentials, employer relationship, or professional license surfaces on inquiry and checks out.
No retention behavior — photos taken casually but not stored or organized; mentions of subject not pursued.
Target ambiguity — multiple subjects observed without focusing on one; pattern fits geographic interest rather than person-targeting.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor can act on knowledge of the subject — combining pattern-of-life mastery, operational security-gap awareness, exploited insider connections (not dormant ones), and the positional ability to reach the subject's environment when the subject is predictably present. Opportunity falls with defensive friction not adapted to, geographic distance not closed, or barriers created by the subject's posture; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: No defensive friction encountered — countermeasures absent or unobserved; actor's behavior continues unimpeded despite organizational posture.

Pattern-of-life mastery — actor reliably locates the subject across schedule, routes, and regular venues; working knowledge of when and where the subject is predictably present. The informational dimension of opportunity.

Geographic-temporal proximity — actor physically lives or works near the subject's environment AND is available during the subject's vulnerable windows. The positional-and-availability dimension. Complementary to pattern-of-life mastery, not redundant: an actor with detailed schedule intelligence but located across the country has reduced opportunity (travel investment required); an actor with proximity but no schedule intel has positional ability without an actionable window.
Operational security-gap knowledge — actor knows patrol rotation times, camera blind spots, shift-change windows, or other facility-specific defender weaknesses.

Insider connection being exploited — identified insider relationship (current or former employee, vendor, social connection) that the actor is actively leveraging for operational intelligence or access gains. Dormant insider connections alone are opportunity potential, not realized opportunity; the EXPLOITATION pattern is what's high-signal.
Direct facility access — actor has unsupervised access to subject-associated facilities through a legitimate role.
low_signal_anchors: Targeting failed against hardened defensive posture — subject's countermeasures actively defeated the actor's approach. Durable signal: the low-opportunity reading is sticky and won't reconstitute without major actor adaptation or posture change.
Institutional rule-out of insider connection — formal access audits or institutional process actively cleared the possibility, not just failed-to-find. High-confidence absence.

Structural access degradation — actor's prior access pathway terminated (role ended, relationship severed, geographic relocation). Distinct from temporary distance: this is a durable structural change.
Defensive friction encountered without adaptation — actor left after being challenged or detected; did not return or adapt approach. Transient signal: may flip back if actor adapts.
Geographic distance not closed — actor across country or region; physical action requires major travel investment that has not been made. Transient: may close if actor commits.

Subject's posture creates effective barriers — subject changed pattern-of-life, hardened venues, or active surveillance detection is working; actor's known methods are blocked. Transient unless durable; depends on whether barriers are sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many legitimate activities produce behaviors that look like this tactic's indicators on the surface — a contractor surveying a site looks similar to a threat actor casing a building; a journalist asking questions looks similar to an actor eliciting information. What distinguishes a false-positive from a real concern is whether the underlying activity has a verifiable legitimate purpose, a transparent identity behind it, or institutional accountability that can be checked.
contexts: Verified professional purpose — journalists, biographers, documentary teams; contractors, vendors, and service providers with site-visit business; real estate professionals on due-diligence visits; appraisers, developers, insurance adjusters, compliance auditors.

Legal authority — authorized law-enforcement or intelligence surveillance with proper legal basis; licensed private investigators on lawful matters; security professionals conducting authorized vulnerability assessments or pen-testing.

Personal or community connection — current and former employees with legitimate facility knowledge (alumni events, retirement visits); neighbors, family, or social connections orienting; new residents or employees in the area.
Non-threatening attention — paparazzi, fans, admirers engaged in invasive but non-threatening behavior; hobbyist photographers.
Academic and research purpose — students researching architecture, urban planning, or history; academic researchers; genealogists; historians with site-visit interests.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings correlating with staging-class behaviors elsewhere — weapon acquisition, observed dry runs, schedule alignment with action windows — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Escalation tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the indicator per the credibility criteria, breadth across modalities, and persistence over time. A single low-credibility indicator with available mundane explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility indicator with operational specificity sits at the investigation tier. Cross-modal corroboration — two or more indicators correlating against the same subject across different observation modes — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as coordinated target-development. Indicators persisting despite implemented countermeasures sit at the committed-actor tier, suggesting potential entry into mobilization. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or modally may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any individual finding warrants in isolation; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered response actions: the monitoring tier triggers logging and pattern-detection workflows; the investigation tier triggers actor-identification effort and subject-vulnerability assessment; the elevation tier triggers countermeasure activation appropriate to the subject's posture; the committed-actor tier triggers defensive-posture upgrade; confirmed actor identity matching a known threat actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor appears at locations associated with the targeted subject on multiple occasions with no apparent legitimate reason
Threat actor conducts reverse image searches, satellite imagery review, or street-view navigation of locations associated with the targeted subject
Threat actor photographs or video-records targeted subject-associated locations including building exteriors, parking access points, security checkpoints, or interior layouts
Threat actor acquires or studies floor plans, blueprints, security camera diagrams, or emergency exit routes for targeted subject-associated locations
Threat actor inquires with current or former employees, security personnel, or facility staff about access procedures, schedules, or targeted subject's routines

countermeasures.measure: Implement varied-route protocols for targeted subject's travel and avoid posting predictable schedules in publicly accessible systems
countermeasures.limitations: Routine may remain observable to a determined threat actor conducting repeated surveillance; this measure raises the cost of pattern-of-life mapping but does not prevent it

countermeasures.measure: Conduct surveillance detection sweeps of protectee-associated locations on a randomized schedule, focusing on persons or vehicles appearing on multiple occasions
countermeasures.limitations: Detection success depends on operator skill and adversary tradecraft; sophisticated subjects rotate observation positions to defeat surveillance detection

countermeasures.measure: Deploy CCTV coverage of approach routes, parking access, and entry points associated with the targeted subject, with retention sufficient to support retrospective pattern analysis
countermeasures.limitations: Recording without active monitoring detects in retrospect, not in time; coverage gaps and aging footage retention limit retrospective value

countermeasures.measure: Conduct digital footprint reduction for the targeted subject including data broker opt-outs, removal of property and address records where legally permitted, establish LLCs and Land Trusts where permitted, and social media privacy hardening
countermeasures.limitations: Public records (court filings, property records, voter registration) cannot be fully removed; partial reduction raises adversary effort but does not eliminate the surface

response_protocols.trigger: One or more Environmental Survey indicators reported (drive-by pattern, reconnaissance imagery, inquiries about targeted subject's routine)
response_protocols.action: Open or update the case file. Conduct a 24-hour preliminary assessment that includes (a) corroboration of the observation, (b) digital footprint review of any identified threat actor, (c) baseline review of recent communications and access requests involving the targeted subject. Document all sourcing.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Threat actor identified with apparent means and proximity to the targeted subject, OR additional indicators across other tactics surface for the same threat actor
response_protocols.legal_notes: Surveillance of an identified threat actor by the organization may have legal implications under privacy and stalking statutes that vary by jurisdiction. Consult counsel before initiating any active monitoring of the threat actor. Document the basis for any investigative action; pretextual or undocumented monitoring creates downstream legal risk.

response_protocols.trigger: Environmental Survey indicators co-observed with credible threat communication, target-specific weapons inquiry, or other Phase 2 mobilization signals
response_protocols.action: Convene the threat management team. Conduct full risk assessment. Notify protective operations and human resources (if subject is internal). Brief executive leadership and consider law-enforcement liaison consult. Implement enhanced protective posture for the targeted subject.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Threat actor confirmed with means and access OR direct or indirect threat communicated.
response_protocols.legal_notes: At this priority tier, parallel notifications to legal and (when applicable) law enforcement are standard. Document the indicator constellation that drove escalation. Preserve evidence of the original observations. Consult counsel on jurisdiction-specific reporting obligations and on privileged-communication scope for the threat management team.

tactics.field_notes: The first signal you usually catch is repetition where there shouldn't be any. Same person at the same coffee shop across the street from the targeted subject's office, three mornings in a row, no apparent business or personal reason. Or a vehicle that appears in the parking garage footage at unusual times. Environmental Survey is rarely a single event you can point to; it's a pattern that resolves over days or weeks of routine observation. Online recon is usually not observed at the time it's happening, so latency is a factor — discovered when preset alerts trigger or after another tactic surfaces and you go back to look at access patterns.
observed_contexts: fixated subject conducting repeated drive-bys of the targeted subject's residence at consistent times
former employee photographing the loading dock and after-hours entry points
stalking case where social media posts revealed the subject had been at the target's gym, restaurant, and church before any direct contact
executive protection case where reverse image search of an open-source post identified the subject standing across from the targeted subject's home
[literature: NTAC-MASS-2021 case pattern — pre-attack site visits in the weeks before mass attacks at workplaces and public venues]

tactics.name: Capability Acquisition
tactics.notes: Actor acquires the means to execute the planned action — weapons, tools, financing, false credentials, vehicles, communications equipment. Capability acquisition is bounded by the planned technique: the acquisition profile reveals the intended method.
tactics.cpn_notes: Dark web procurement, cryptocurrency for anonymous purchasing, and online forgery services are the primary acquisition channels for many capability types. Encrypted communications enable coordination with suppliers without generating conventional financial or communications records.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor acquires weapons, ammunition, or restricted equipment in quantities or configurations inconsistent with hobbyist or sporting use, particularly in a compressed time window
Threat actor purchases or rents vehicles, tools, or equipment that have no apparent legitimate use in their declared activities, especially items operationally relevant to the planned attack method
Threat actor obtains or attempts to obtain access credentials, uniforms, identification documents, or workplace keys outside the scope of their legitimate role
Threat actor leverages a third party — family member, friend, employee — to acquire an item the threat actor cannot legally or practically obtain directly
Threat actor researches modification, conversion, or improvised construction of attack capability — including 3D-printed firearm components, IED precursor combinations, or vehicle modifications
Threat actor accesses workplace inventory, supply rooms, or restricted storage outside the scope of declared duties to obtain attack-relevant items

countermeasures.measure: Implement structured background and continuous-evaluation programs for personnel in roles with access to attack-relevant materials, with reporting obligations for behavioral changes
countermeasures.limitations: Background checks are point-in-time; continuous evaluation requires sustained funding and workforce buy-in. Family-member acquisition pathways are not addressed by personnel programs

countermeasures.measure: Deliver household firearm and equipment safety briefings for the targeted subject and immediate family, including expectations for reporting unauthorized access by extended family or guests
countermeasures.limitations: Awareness fades; family members may resist treating relatives as suspects. Effectiveness depends on the household's existing security culture

countermeasures.measure: Maintain workplace inventory and access-log monitoring with anomaly detection for restricted storage, particularly for keys, uniforms, identification, and equipment that maps to known attack capabilities
countermeasures.limitations: Insiders with legitimate access may not trigger alerts. Inventory baselines must be accurate before anomalies can be detected

countermeasures.measure: Train associates and family members on proxy-purchase warning indicators, including unusual requests to buy items outside the requester's normal interests
countermeasures.limitations: Many proxy purchases appear benign in isolation and are only recognizable when combined with other concerning context the proxy may not have

response_protocols.trigger: Single capability acquisition indicator detected (unusual purchase, anomalous workplace inventory access, peer-reported request for proxy assistance)
response_protocols.action: Document the indicator. Conduct a 5-business-day preliminary assessment that includes (a) corroboration of the observation, (b) financial-pattern review where authorized and available, (c) baseline review of the threat actor's prior acquisition history. Determine whether the acquisition profile maps to a coherent attack method.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Acquisition profile maps coherently to a specific attack method OR concurrent indicators surface from another Phase 1 tactic for the same threat actor.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Personal acquisition history may have privacy implications; coordinate with legal before any direct inquiry. Workplace acquisition data is generally accessible under normal security policy. Document the basis for any monitoring escalation. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

response_protocols.trigger: Multiple acquisition indicators consistent with attack capability OR single high-severity indicator (illegal weapon acquisition, IED precursor combinations, restricted-access credential theft)
response_protocols.action: Convene the threat management team within 24 hours. Conduct formal threat assessment. Implement protective posture for the targeted subject. Notify law enforcement where the acquisition itself is unlawful or where jurisdiction requires reporting. Initiate enhanced monitoring of the threat actor across available data sources.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Threat actor demonstrates means and proximity to the targeted subject OR direct communication of intent to use acquired capability.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Illegal weapon acquisition and certain IED precursor combinations carry mandatory reporting obligations in many jurisdictions. Document the indicator constellation that drove escalation. Preserve evidence of the original observations. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

tactics.field_notes: Capability Acquisition resolves into three pathways: legitimate purchase (firearms transfer through licensed dealers, vehicle rentals, equipment from retailers), theft or diversion (workplace theft of credentials, building keys, or equipment; family-member firearm taken without consent), and proxy procurement (a third party purchases the capability on the threat actor's behalf, sometimes wittingly, often not). Each pathway leaves a different signature. Legitimate purchases surface in financial records and background-check databases; theft surfaces in workplace inventory or peer reports of missing items; proxy procurement surfaces in associate interviews and after-incident analysis of who actually bought what. The detection difficulty rises sharply across the three: a threat assessment team can routinely catch legitimate purchases through structured data; proxy procurement is often only recognizable in retrospect. The acquisition profile usually reveals the intended attack method — what was acquired, in what combination, on what timeline.
observed_contexts: workplace violence case where the threat actor purchased a firearm from a licensed dealer and ammunition from multiple retailers within a three-week window before the attack
domestic case where the threat actor accessed a household firearm belonging to a family member, with no purchase trail of their own to identify
insider threat case where the threat actor used legitimate workplace access to remove uniforms, ID badges, and a contractor vehicle key in the weeks preceding mobilization
[literature: NTAC-MASS-2021 — pre-attack acquisition timelines for mass attacks against public spaces, including weapons, vehicles, and protective gear]
extremist radicalization case where the threat actor researched 3D-printed firearm components and IED precursors online for months before any physical acquisition occurred

credibility.criteria: Credibility of a Capability Acquisition finding rises with recoverable transactional evidence — financial, rental, delivery, and access records — that physically ties the actor to the materiel, with corroboration across separate acquisition threads, and with an anomaly of quantity, configuration, or timing that lawful use does not account for. It falls with uncorroborated single reports, acquisitions that have a checkable lawful purpose, an ordinary explanation left unaddressed, and reporters whose stake could distort the account.
high_signal_anchors: Recoverable transactional evidence — financial, rental, delivery, or access records that physically tie the actor to the materiel, independent of how well a witness remembers.
An anomaly without an ordinary explanation — a quantity, configuration, or compressed timing of acquisition that lawful hobby, sporting, or occupational use does not account for.
Corroboration across acquisition threads — separate acquisitions of materiel, access means, and technical knowledge converging toward one operational capability.
A proxy relationship surfaced first-hand — a named third party who can confirm being asked to obtain something on the actor's behalf.
Operational matching of what was obtained — acquired items that fit together into a coherent attack means rather than unrelated purchases.
Reporter standing aligned with accuracy — the account reaches the assessor through a channel with no structural stake in the outcome.
low_signal_anchors: A single uncorroborated report — one tip, with no transactional record and no second acquisition thread.
An acquisition with a checkable lawful purpose — the materiel fits a verifiable hobby, occupation, or sporting activity that investigation confirms.
An ordinary explanation left standing — the purchase or access fits a mundane account the assessment never actually ruled out.
Reporter stake that could distort — the person raising the concern is inside an active dispute or proceeding with the actor.
Reconstructive recall — a long delay between the acquisition and the report, where detail may be retrofitted to a threatening narrative.
An isolated, unmatched purchase — a single item with no operational relationship to any other acquisition or to a method.

capability.criteria: Capability is a high-signal dimension for Capability Acquisition — this is the tactic in which an actor's capacity to carry out a threat materially crystallizes. It is read less from the sophistication of the acquisition itself, which is usually only moderate, than from what has been obtained: the lethality of the materiel, how completely it assembles into a functioning attack means, and whether the actor has converted acquired items from latent to operational. It falls where acquisitions are incomplete, untested, mismatched to any method, or remain ordinary dual-use items with no operational configuration.
high_signal_anchors: Lethal means obtained — the actor has acquired weapons, ammunition, or materials whose realistic use is the infliction of serious harm.
An attack means assembling toward completeness — separate acquisitions combining into a functioning capability rather than isolated items.
Acquired materiel matched to a method — what has been obtained corresponds to a specific, coherent way of carrying out an attack.
Capability converted from latent to operational — acquired items prepared, modified, tested, or assembled into working order rather than left as purchased.

Capability the actor is building rather than buying — research or practice aimed at producing or improvising a means the actor cannot readily obtain ready-made, raising the ceiling of what they could field.
A barrier to acquisition overcome — materiel obtained that the actor could not lawfully or readily get, whether through a proxy, an exploited access route, or improvisation.
low_signal_anchors: Dual-use items with no operational configuration — acquisitions that remain ordinary and could serve any number of lawful purposes.
Incomplete or mismatched acquisition — items obtained that do not assemble into, or correspond to, any coherent attack means.
Untested, unprepared materiel — acquired items left as purchased, with no sign of being made operational.
A single ordinary purchase — one item, lawfully obtained, with no anomaly of quantity, configuration, or timing.
Aspirational interest without acquisition — attack means discussed or admired but with no materiel obtained and no construction attempted.

intent.criteria: Intent is a high-signal dimension for Capability Acquisition — committing money, effort, and risk to obtain the means of an attack is among the least ambiguous intent signals in the threat pathway. Intent rises with acquisition that is operationally specific to a method, with effort or exposure taken on to overcome a barrier, with materiel assembled in a compressed timeframe, and with acquisition that follows expressed grievance and target development. It falls with acquisitions that have a verifiable benign purpose, with ordinary dual-use purchases, and with interest in capability that produces no acquisition.
high_signal_anchors: Resources committed to attack means — money, effort, or legal exposure expended to obtain materiel whose purpose is an attack.
Operational specificity of the acquisition — what is obtained corresponds to a particular method rather than to general preparedness.
A barrier deliberately overcome — the actor took on the effort or exposure of a proxy, an exploited access route, or improvisation to get something they could not obtain directly.
Acquisition compressed in time — materiel assembled rapidly rather than accumulated slowly, indicating a timeline behind the activity.
Acquisition following grievance and target development — capability obtained by an actor who has already expressed hostility toward, and profiled, a subject.
Concealment of the acquisition — purchases routed, disguised, or proxied in a way that signals the actor's own awareness the acquisition would not be sanctioned.
low_signal_anchors: A verifiable benign purpose — the acquisition fits a checkable hobby, occupation, or lawful activity.
Ordinary dual-use purchasing — items with broad lawful uses and no operational configuration toward an attack.
Capability interest without acquisition — attack means discussed or researched but nothing obtained.
An isolated purchase with no pattern — a single acquisition with no anomaly, no method match, and no other acquisition thread.
Long-standing lawful collecting — materiel accumulated over years consistent with a known hobby, not assembled toward a timeline.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity is a lower-signal dimension for Capability Acquisition — most of the tactic concerns the means of an attack rather than access to the subject, and acquiring materiel resolves little about whether the actor can reach the target. Opportunity registers in this tactic only through its access sub-thread: where the actor obtains credentials, identification, or keys, or exploits insider standing to reach restricted environments. It stays low wherever the finding concerns materiel alone.
high_signal_anchors: Means of entry obtained — the actor has acquired credentials, identification, or keys that would let them pass into a controlled environment.
Insider standing exploited for reach — the actor turning a position of legitimate access, used outside its scope, into reach the actor's role would not otherwise allow.
Access acquisition matched to the target environment — the credentials or access obtained correspond to the subject's workplace or controlled setting.
Acquisition that itself creates proximity — obtaining a role, vehicle, or relationship that places the actor in or near the subject's environment.
low_signal_anchors: Materiel acquisition only — weapons, tools, or equipment obtained, resolving nothing about reaching the subject.
Capability research with no access dimension — technical study of attack means that carries no information about proximity or entry.
Generic access with no target match — credentials or access obtained that do not correspond to the subject's environment.
No indication of reach — nothing in the finding suggests the actor can convert acquired capability into proximity to the subject.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many ordinary activities resemble Capability Acquisition indicators on the surface — lawful firearms ownership, hobby and occupational purchasing, vehicle and tool acquisition, and routine workplace access all produce surface-similar behavior. What separates a false positive from a concern is whether the acquisition has a verifiable lawful purpose, whether the quantity, configuration, and timing are consistent with that purpose, whether the items assemble toward an attack means, and whether access obtained stays within the actor's legitimate role.
contexts: Lawful firearms and sporting ownership — hunters, sport shooters, and collectors acquiring and holding weapons and ammunition consistent with a documented, long-standing activity.
Hobby, trade, and occupational purchasing — tradespeople, hobbyists, makers, and professionals buying tools, chemicals, vehicles, or equipment their work or pastime ordinarily requires.
Ordinary vehicle and equipment acquisition — buying or renting a vehicle, tools, or gear for relocation, a project, or recreation, with no operational relationship to a subject.
Legitimate workplace access — employees drawing on credentials, keys, and storage within the scope of their actual duties.
Maker and technical hobby interest — 3D printing, electronics, chemistry, and fabrication pursued as a documented hobby or course of study, with no movement toward a weapon or a subject.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Capability Acquisition findings show whether an actor is obtaining the means to carry out an attack — the point in the pathway where intent becomes materially equipped. The key reading is whether what has been acquired assembles toward a functioning attack means, and how completely. Tier determination rests on three factors: credibility per the credibility criteria, the lethality and operational specificity of what has been acquired, and whether the acquisition shows a compressed timeframe. A single low-credibility acquisition with a verifiable lawful purpose sits at a monitoring tier. A single high-credibility finding — lethal materiel obtained, a barrier deliberately overcome, or insider access acquired to a controlled environment — sits at an investigation tier. Convergence — materiel, access means, and technical capability assembling toward one coherent attack means — sits at an elevation tier and should be treated as active mobilization. Acquisition in a compressed timeframe, or capability converted from latent to operational, sits at a committed-actor tier and indicates the intervention window is closing.
